transcript:
Meeting header: HeliosGrid x Redwood Inference discovery
Date: 2025-10-03
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Roberto Diaz (Redwood SE), Leah Park (Redwood CSM), Tom Nguyen (Redwood SE), Priya Kaur (HeliosGrid Head of ML), Elliot Marsh (HeliosGrid SRE), Samir Patel (HeliosGrid CISO), Naomi Lee (HeliosGrid Platform)
Shared: Deck: https://redwood.app/decks/dedicated-overview (shared by Maya), Benchmark sheet link noted in chat

00:00 Maya: Hey everyone thanks for joining, cadence, so we'll do a quick intro, then dig into HeliosGrid's workload and constraints, and then read through dedicated options and burst model, is that right Priya?
00:12 Priya: Yeah that sounds good. Thanks, uh Maya. Quick note, Naomi's on mute but she'll chime in on the network side.
00:20 Roberto: Hi all, Roberto from infra, I'll focus on latency/cost tradeoffs and prewarm behavior.
00:28 Elliot: Elliot here, SRE; our main goal is predictable latency under burst traffic and safe isolation between teams.
00:34 Samir: And I'm Samir, I'll ask the security and compliance questions, mostly around KMS and audit logs.

01:05 Maya: Cool, can you give us an overview of current traffic? peak qps, average tokens per request, percent of long sessions?
01:12 Priya: Sure. On average 700 qps, peaks at about 3.2k for short windows. Tokens per request is bimodal — 30 tokens for chat assistants and about 800 tokens for doc-summarization batch jobs. Long sessions are maybe 8% of total.
01:28 Naomi: Important detail, our external customers expect sub-250ms p50 for the chat surface, but batch jobs can tolerate more latency.
01:40 Roberto: That split matters for batching and for dedicated warm pools. If you have many short requests, batching could help but we also need low p50 so can't overbatch.

03:05 Priya: We're evaluating hosted first but have strict data residency and some compliance customers that require VPC or on-prem isolation. So Dedicated/VPC or Private is in scope.
03:20 Maya: Got it. For Dedicated we do a Dedicated pool inside our infra with VPC peering and customer-managed subnets; Private is full on-prem. Which path do you prefer long term?
03:32 Priya: Ideally Dedicated with VPC peering — quicker to onboard and keeps control of keys.

04:10 Samir: A few security asks: can Redwood integrate with our AWS KMS and HSM? Do you provide per-tenant encryption keys, and how do audit logs look?
04:21 Tom: Yes we support KMS integrations for Dedicated and Private. Audit logs include request metadata, model versions, and routing decisions; we can push to your CloudWatch or S3. There's an enterprise add-on for longer retention.
04:40 Samir: Ok, also do you rotate keys, and is there a BYOK option?
04:46 Tom: BYOK is supported for Private and Dedicated via Customer-Managed KMS. Key rotation is customer-controlled.

06:00 Maya: Let's talk isolation. How many teams/tenants, and what are failure blast-radius concerns?
06:07 Priya: Right now 12 internal product tenants plus a few external partner tenants. We want compute-level isolation for partners and soft-tenancy for internal teams. Preemption is not acceptable for partners.
06:20 Roberto: We can propose a mix: segregated GPU pools for external partners, multi-tenant pools with strict cgroups/namespace limits for internal teams. For preemption, Dedicated reserved nodes won't be preempted, but if you opt for burst to shared capacity there can be fallbacks.

07:05 Elliot: How does Redwood handle burst? We want quick ramp from 700 to 3.2k qps in under 2 minutes ideally.
07:13 Roberto: We use warm-pools (hot-pools) plus prewarmed containers. Typical prewarm times depend on model size; for a 70B model full warm-up can take 40–90s but we mitigate with snapshotting KV caches and hybrid prewarm strategies.
07:30 Priya: Snapshotting KV cache, is that something you expose?
07:34 Roberto: Yeah, we call it prefix/KV cache snapshots in the runtime — not always perfect in transcriptions I'll call it KV caching. We can restore a cache into a warm node to reduce first-token latency.

09:00 Naomi: About networking: VPC peering latency, egress controls, are there any egress costs or double traversal?
09:10 Tom: VPC peering is straightforward; traffic flows inside your AWS VPC. For Dedicated in region, egress is typically internal; we can also provide direct connect options for Private.

10:05 Samir: From compliance perspective, do you have SOC 2 type II? Any ISO or HIPAA experience?
10:11 Maya: Redwood has SOC 2 Type II; Private deployments have additional controls and we have customers in healthcare — we can share the compliance pack.

11:30 Priya: Cost — what's the unit economics? We care about tokens per second cost and price for reserved GPUs vs on-demand.
11:39 Maya: Pricing: reserved capacity has a committed monthly fee plus lower per-token runtime. Hosted on-demand is higher tick price. We'll send a pricing matrix but ballpark 40–60% savings at scale for reservedDedicated versus hosted.
11:58 Priya: And for burst? Is burst metered differently?
12:04 Roberto: Burst uses either dedicated burst reserved headroom (if you purchase burst units) or routes to shared capacity at a different price tier. We can create a hybrid plan where you pay for a modest reserved pool and an overflow rate.

13:00 Elliot: Any GC/eviction policies for KV caches? If we scale down does the cache dump to S3?
13:08 Roberto: Caches can be snapshot to S3 or to an internal cache store; snapshot/restore times are measured in seconds to low minutes depending on model and sequence length. There's tradeoff between snapshot size and restore time.

15:00 Priya: Model versions and rollouts — we need canarying and A/B testing across model variants and quantized profiles.
15:08 Tom: Redwood supports rollouts in Console with traffic split, and you can pin model versions. We also have an Optimize tool that suggests quantization and batching config per workload.

17:00 Maya: For your 800-token job patterns, do you want to run those on a different model family (quantized) to save cost?
17:08 Priya: Possibly — quality is important for summarization though, so we might accept slight quality hit for cost savings but need evals.
17:20 Maya: We'll propose a dual pipeline: chat on low-latency family, batch summarization on quantized high-throughput family.

19:00 Naomi: On onboarding timeline — how long to provision Dedicated with VPC peering and KMS? we're looking at October end or early November window.
19:10 Maya: Typical lead time 2–4 weeks for standard Dedicated. If you want reserved nodes with guaranteed SLA and custom KMS integration, plan for 3–6 weeks depending on signed contract and network reviews.
19:26 Priya: We have regulatory customers so we may need Private later, what's the delta on lead time for Private?
19:33 Tom: Private is longer — 8–12 weeks for on-prem with air-gapped packaging, but shorter if you're doing Dedicated in your VPC.

21:00 Elliot: Latency SLOs — you mentioned p50/p95 targets earlier; can you guarantee p95 < 700ms for chat under peak?
21:10 Roberto: SLA targets depend on reserved footprint and warm strategy. With sufficient reserved warm nodes sized for peak and KV caching we can get p95 in the 400–600ms ballpark for short prompts; we'll need to run an arrival-rate-based sizing sim.

23:00 Priya: We also have multi-region needs — US and EU. Can we have reserved pools in both regions and cross-region fallback?
23:10 Tom: Yes, multi-region reserved is supported with routing policies; we can also configure automatic fallback to a lower-cost region but you'll have to think about data residency and latency tradeoffs.

25:00 Samir: Audit logs detail — can we get request-level metadata stripped of PII for retention 7 years?
25:12 Tom: We can redact payloads and retain metadata; long retention is an add-on. We'll share the retention options in the compliance pack.

27:00 Priya: One blocker for us is tenant isolation for partners. We need hard-gated resource guarantees and no noisy neighbor.
27:10 Roberto: For that we recommend physical segregation: dedicated GPU pools per partner or per partner group, with network ACLs and IAM mapping. That adds cost but minimizes blast radius.

29:00 Naomi: How does your console surface token-level cost — can our finance export token spend per product line?
29:08 Leah: Console has token-level breakdowns and route tagging; you can export CSVs and integrate billing webhooks to feed your internal chargeback systems.

31:00 Priya: For the burst ramp test, can we run a POC benchmark with our traces?
31:07 Maya: Absolutely. Next step is a scoped POC: HeliosGrid provides 7 days of traces, Redwood runs a replay in a dedicated test harness and shares latency/costs under different warm pool sizes.
31:20 Priya: How long does the POC take?
31:23 Roberto: Usually 1–2 weeks depending on trace complexity. We'll run both steady-state and spike tests.

33:00 Elliot: On failure modes — if a prewarm snapshot fails what happens to in-flight requests?
33:07 Roberto: We fall back to a compatible model variant or route to hosted fallback; that increases latency but keeps service available. We have circuit-breakers and graceful degradation policies.

35:00 Samir: Encryption in transit and at rest — is TLS mutual supported and do you sign certs for peering?
35:07 Tom: TLS mutual can be configured for Private and Dedicated; cert management is via your PKI or we can provide options.

37:00 Priya: Any rate-limit patterns — token bucket, per-route limits? we want per-tenant shaping to avoid noisy neighbor.
37:08 Leah: Yes, we support per-route and per-key rate limits and quotas. You can set soft and hard limits and callbacks for throttled requests.

39:00 Naomi: The team also asked about GPU types — do you support A100 vs H100 and how do model kernels differ?
39:08 Roberto: We support both. H100 typically gives better throughput for large models; kernel selection and compilation is automatic but we'll recommend instance types per model. We'll include perf matrix.

41:00 Priya: One more: evictions/policy for reserved vs burst — do you let customers set priority levels?
41:08 Roberto: Yes, we expose priority tiers: pinned reserved, reserved, burst-on-demand. You can set tenant priority and fallback policies.

43:00 Maya: Quick recap — HeliosGrid wants Dedicated with VPC peering, BYOK KMS, segregated pools for external partners, warm-pool prewarm for quick spikes, and a POC to run traces. Action items and next steps in chat. Anything else?
43:20 Priya: That's it from my side. Thanks.
43:24 Samir: I'll send our compliance list.
43:30 Maya: Great, we'll send pricing, POC plan and schedule the deep technical dive.

Closing notes: References shared: Dedicated deck (link above), Benchmark sheet (private link in chat), Compliance pack request (Maya to attach).

End of transcript.
